head: The Shapiros Have Been Boo'ed!
sub: A sneaky Halloween visitor was caught on the doorbell camera, and the Scoop has a suspect
story: Somebody crept up to the Shapiro house with a spooky surprise: the Shapiros have been Boo'ed! Being Boo'ed is a Halloween tradition. A secret visitor leaves treats at a neighbor's door, often with a sign that says "You've been Boo'ed!", and then tiptoes away before anyone sees.

But this visitor was not quite sneaky enough. The doorbell camera snapped the picture you see here. After a careful investigation, the Scoop has one prime suspect: Madeline Minken. Take a close look at the photo. Does that look like a booer to you?

Getting Boo'ed comes with a job. A family that gets Boo'ed keeps the fun going by secretly Boo-ing someone else, so the treats travel around the neighborhood all the way to Halloween. Who will the Shapiros Boo next? Whoever it is had better watch out for doorbell cameras!

head: Squeeze Me! A Juice Machine Does the Squeezing
sub: At Nino Salvaggio's in Bloomfield, shoppers fill their own bottles with fresh orange juice
story: There is a new machine at Nino Salvaggio's in Bloomfield, and it is all about oranges. A big wire basket on top is piled high with whole oranges. They drop into the machine, where they are cut in half and squeezed right in front of you. Peek through the window and you can watch the orange halves get pressed!

A sign next to the machine shows how to build your own bottle in four steps. Grab an empty bottle from the rack. Set it under the spout. Hold the push button down until the bottle is full of fresh juice. Then tighten the cap. Each bottle holds 16 ounces and costs $7.99.

The juice is unpasteurized, which means it has not been heated, so it tastes like a just-picked orange. That also means it has to stay cold, so keep it in the refrigerator. Already-filled bottles wait on ice nearby for anyone in a hurry. Would you rather squeeze your own or grab one from the ice?

head: A Piece of a Rocket Company for Every Kid?
sub: Elon Musk says he will give one SpaceX share to every child in America next year, but the details aren't out yet
story: Elon Musk, who runs the rocket company SpaceX, made a big promise on Monday. "Next year, I will give one of my SpaceX shares to every kid in America," he wrote on X. "This will be the first of many." That could mean kids just like you!

A share is a tiny piece of a company. Owning one share of SpaceX would make you the owner of a very small part of the company that builds rockets like the Falcon 9 and Starship. SpaceX started selling shares to the public in June, and at the end of last week one share was worth about $146. When a company does well, its shares can be worth more; when it doesn't, they can be worth less.

There are about 73 million kids under 18 in the United States, so the gift would add up to about $10.7 billion. Mr. Musk hasn't said yet how kids would get their shares, exactly when it will happen, or who counts as a kid, so grown-ups will be watching for the details. What would you do if you owned a piece of a rocket company?
head_src: Fox Business and CNN (via Yahoo Finance), Oct. 19, 2026
